after.worked_solution:
If we have a data set that consists of the points ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n},$ then the variance can be computed as

$$
{\sigma }^{2}=\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}-(\overset{―}{x})^{2},
$$

where $\overset{―}{x}$ is the mean of the data set and $\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}$ is the mean of the squares of the points in the data set.

First, let's compute $\overset{―}{x}.$ There are $n=10$ points in our data set, and we know that ${\sum }_{i=1}^{10}{x}_{i}=-110,$ so we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{x} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{10}{\sum }_{i=1}^{10}{x}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{10}\cdot (-110) \\  & =-11.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, let's compute $\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}.$ We know that ${\sum }_{i=1}^{10}{x}_{i}^{2}=1\,350,$ so we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{{x}^{2}} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{10}{\sum }_{i=1}^{10}{x}_{i}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{10}\cdot 1350 \\  & =135.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the variance is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }^{2} & =\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}-(\overset{―}{x})^{2} \\  & =135-{(-11)}^{2} \\  & =135-121 \\  & =14.\end{aligned}
$$
